B. Is this measure already running in Lapland wellbeing services county (or in the OYS university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Our model assumes no direct effect on patients for this measure. Instead: does a source you read document the problem it fixes?
Measure: Audit of treatment records ("no treatment on record"). Take 50 patients with no treatment on record and check the charts: were they untreated, or was drug treatment or radiotherapy given and not coded? Fix the coding. It treats no extra patient, but until it is done the county cannot tell a care gap from a recording gap.
effect_summary_en: The Cancer Registry lung cancer report documents the recording problem: stage at diagnosis was missing for about half of patients (48 %), and the curative-treatment share was lower than the national share in the Northern Finland collaborative area; the model's zero direct effect is an assumption.
supported_en: The Cancer Registry report shows stage missing for 48 % of lung cancer patients and a lower curative-treatment share in Northern Finland.
not_supported_en: No page shows how much of Lapland's "no treatment on record" share is a recording gap rather than a care gap.
summary_en: Lapland county (lapha.fi) and OYS pages show no public sign of an audit of "no treatment on record" cases; the county's cancer page says only that Lapland patients get radiotherapy at OYS. The national Cancer Registry lung cancer report finds stage missing for 48 % of patients and a lower curative-treatment share in the Northern Finland collaborative area. That is the gap between real care and recorded care that this audit would sort out.
unanswered_en: Over three search rounds I found no Lapland or OYS page on auditing treatment records or on how well they report to the Cancer Registry.
